Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi (commonly known as Mahatma Gandhi) was born on 2 October 1869 in Porbandar, India. He became the leader of the Indian independence movement against British rule, pioneering the philosophy of non‑violent resistance (Satyagraha). Gandhi’s efforts helped India gain independence in 1947. He is remembered worldwide for his commitment to truth, simplicity, and civil disobedience, and he is often called “the Father of the Nation” in India. He was assassinated on 30 January 1948.

tell me about sun

The Sun is the star at the center of our Solar System. It’s a middle‑aged G‑type main‑sequence star, about 4.6 billion years old, with a diameter of roughly 1.4 million km (≈109 Earth diameters). Its core, where nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium occurs, generates the energy that powers the Sun and radiates outward as visible light, ultraviolet, and other electromagnetic waves. The Sun’s mass (≈1.99 × 10²⁶ kg) dominates the Solar System’s gravity, keeping the planets in orbit. It has a layered structure: core, radiative zone, convective zone, photosphere (visible surface), chromosphere, and corona (hot outer atmosphere). The Sun’s magnetic activity drives phenomena such as sunspots, solar flares, and coronal mass ejections, which can affect space weather and Earth’s technology.
